title: 2 BOXES OF CHINA INCLUDING CAR...
reason: Five or six Carlton Ware Apple Blossom style pieces (leaf dishes, jug, cruet set) plus other porcelain; collectable maker but a common pattern in Australia, so modest value
findings: One photo of about 25 pieces laid out. The Carltonware claim is supported by the look of five pieces: moulded leaf shaped ware with brown woven (basket weave) handles and pink and cream star shaped blossoms with yellow centres and green leaves, which matches the Carlton Ware 'Apple Blossom' range (registered Australian design, 1930s to 50s); I compared with a dealer's reference photo, but the pattern name is unconfirmed. They are: a large green triangular leaf dish, a green oval leaf bowl with handle, a yellow triangular leaf tray holding a matching pair of egg shaped salt and pepper shakers (a cruet set), a small green leaf dish with handle, and a green cream jug with a woven handle. A cream shell shaped dish with a blue and pink floral spray plus a spoon sits in a green patterned presentation box, possibly also Carlton Ware but unconfirmed. Other pieces: about a dozen small cream jugs and jugs (mostly gilt edged porcelain with floral bands, one hand painted with red flowers on black and cream), a red and gilt decorated cup and saucer in Japanese style, a gilt edged handled cake plate with pink rose borders, a round scenic lake and mountain plate on a stand, a cream moulded fan shaped dish with orange roses, a small figural jug (man in green coat and hat), a small cream vase with orange handles, and a mottled pottery pot. No backstamps or marks are visible because only fronts are shown, so the Carlton Ware attribution cannot be checked from the bases.
condition: No chips, cracks or hairlines visible from the front in one photo; gilding looks worn on some pieces; bases, handles' undersides and inside rims are not shown and crazing cannot be assessed.
rescore_note: About five or six pieces that look like Carlton Ware leaf ware with woven handles (cruet set, jug, leaf dishes) plus assorted gilt porcelain; attribution rests on looks only with no backstamps shown, the pattern is common here, and bases and crazing are unseen, so mid band. No new price comps checked (search limit reached).
